title: Rollout Lens Sequencer: Temporal Diffing for Canary, A/B and Shadow Traffic
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Operators need a single, time-aware workspace in Console to compare behavior across rollout variants (canary/A/B/shadow) for a given route, surface regressions early, and recommend safe auto-rollback actions. Current Console views are scattered: metrics dashboards, trace lists, and cohort diffs live in separate panels with limited temporal alignment.

Goal: Build the 'Rollout Lens Sequencer' — a per-route, temporal diffing workspace that stitches metric series, sample traces, and response diffs across cohorts into synchronized timelines. The workspace should: 1) support side-by-side and overlay comparisons for metrics (latency, success, token-cost, hallucination rate), 2) show representative traces and request/response snapshots aligned to the same time window, 3) surface statistically significant deltas with suggested rollback severity (none / soft / immediate), and 4) integrate with shadow traffic playback for post-hoc divergence analysis.

Why this matters: Faster detection of model regressions reduces customer-visible errors and cost. By correlating trace-level anomalies with cohort-level metric deltas, SREs and product engineers can decide rollbacks with higher confidence, lowering mean time to remediation and the frequency of unnecessary rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows a new 'Lens Sequencer' view accessible from per-route Rollouts page
Users can select up to 3 cohorts/variants and a time window and see synchronized metric timelines (p75/p95 latency, error rate, tokens per request, hallucination score)
Lens presents a ranked list of significant deltas with p-values and effect sizes and maps each delta to candidate rollback recommendations (none / gradual / immediate)
Each highlighted metric delta links to filtered traces and 10 representative request/response samples for the same time range
Shadow traffic playback: ability to replay a sampled slice of shadowed requests against the canary variant and visualize divergence score distribution
Integrations: clicking a suggested rollback opens the existing Rollout Orchestrator modal pre-filled with route, variant, and rollback severity
Telemetry hooks are instrumented so that rollbacks triggered via the Lens generate an audit event and a revertable change in the rollout timeline
success_metrics: Time-to-detection reduced from median 27m to <=10m for P1 regressions
False-positive rollback suggestions reduced by 30% (measured via rollback reversal rate)
80% of canary incidents have a linked representative trace within the Lens view
Adoption: 40% of active teams use Lens within 2 weeks of release for canary/A-B investigations
technical_requirements: Aggregation: time-aligned metric buckets (1m/5m) for per-variant series with bootstrapped significance tests
Trace linking: store pointers to trace IDs for top anomalous requests per bucket; sample size cap at 200 traces per query
Response diffs: lightweight structured diffing that can flag token-level divergences and hallucination-score deltas
Auth: obey per-customer RBAC and ensure private deployment compatibility (no PII leakage in shared views)
Performance: API responses must render the view within 1.2s for a 24h window and 3 variants
ui_notes: Layout: three-pane UX: left = variants selector + cohort summary, center = synchronized metric timelines, right = trace & sample inspector
Timeline controls: zoom, brush selection for ad-hoc time windows, and 'step' arrows to jump to next significant delta
Delta badges: color-coded (green/yellow/red) with hover explanation and CTA to open rollback modal
Accessibility: keyboard-first navigation for time-scrubbing and variant switching
Design files: https://figma.redwood.ai/file/rollout-lens-sequencer (attached mocks and responsive states)
backend_tasks: ENG-82145: Implement RolloutLens API and pagination for trace pointers
ENG-82201: Metric aggregator service changes to emit per-variant bucketed stats and bootstrap p-values
ENG-82234: Response-diff microservice that computes lightweight token divergence and hallucination metrics
ENG-82310: Hook audit log events for rollback action initiated from Lens
ENG-82402: Add authorization checks so private deployments filter sensitive samples
telemetry_queries: Example metric delta query: SELECT variant, time_bucket, p50_latency, p95_latency, count FROM rollout_variant_buckets WHERE route='payment-parse' AND time BETWEEN ? AND ?
Significance test pseudocode: bootstrap(samples_variantA, samples_variantB) -> distribution of mean_diffs -> p-value
Trace selector: index:trace_events where variant_tag=canary AND status!='ok' ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 200
Divergence score: compute token-wise BLEU/Levenshtein plus hallucination model score averaged per-sample
rollout_plan: Week 1: API design review and perf budget sign-off; finalize UI mocks with design
Week 2: Implement metric bucketing + significance engine and basic timeline rendering (backend + stubbed UI)
Week 3: Trace linking, sample response diffs, and rollback integration; internal dogfood on staging (two teams)
Week 4: Shadow playback integration and private deployment testing; GA rollout to 20% of accounts with opt-in flag
Post-GA: iterate on delta ranking thresholds, QA fixes, and onboarding docs (playbook for SREs)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy significance alerts from low-volume routes -> Mitigation: require minimum N requests per cohort and expose adjustable sensitivity slider
Risk: exposing PII in sampled requests -> Mitigation: auto-mask request text using configured redaction rules and apply private deployment filters
Risk: performance regression on console -> Mitigation: lazy-load trace samples, cache metric buckets for 5m windows, and enforce 1.2s rendering SLO
Risk: misguided auto-rollback recommendations -> Mitigation: conservative default thresholds and require human confirmation for immediate rollbacks; log rationale in audit
